extracted.intended_audience: recipients of federal financial assistance (educational institutions), Title IX Coordinators, school administrators, compliance officers, and legal counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted guidance and regulatory standards governing when and how recipients (schools, colleges) may offer and implement informal resolution under 34 C.F.R. §106.44(k), including limits, required notices, voluntariness, facilitator qualifications, recordkeeping, and related guardrails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretion to offer informal resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may offer to a complainant and respondent an informal resolution process, subject to the limitations in paragraph (k)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department gives recipients discretion to offer informal resolution within §106.44(k)'s guardrails; discretion is not unfettered and must be exercised in a manner that treats the parties equitably (consistent with §106.44(f)(1)(i)). Recipients may decline to offer informal resolution in appropriate fact-specific circumstances (e.g., risk of future harm, repeated allegations, identity/role of parties), but are not required to provide written reasons for declining.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition for employee-to-minor sex-based harassment
rubrics_metrics.description: Informal resolution is prohibited if the complaint includes allegations that an employee engaged in sex-based harassment of an elementary school or secondary school student.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule narrows the originally-proposed broader prohibition; it applies only to K–12 students and only to sex-based harassment (due to the unique risks of physical harm and severe emotional trauma). The prohibition does not extend to postsecondary students, including student-employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable information threshold for offering informal resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient has discretion to determine whether it is appropriate to offer an informal resolution process when it receives information about conduct that 'reasonably' may constitute sex discrimination under Title IX 'or this part.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department added the word 'reasonably' to §106.44(k)(1)(i). Recipients have flexibility to structure how they assess whether information reasonably indicates potential sex discrimination; facts and circumstances (history of violent conduct, credible threats, etc.) may inform the assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary consent; prohibition on requiring or pressuring participation
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must not require or pressure a party to participate in informal resolution, and informal resolution cannot be pursued unless both parties voluntarily consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule explicitly forbids requiring or pressuring (positive or negative) parties to use informal resolution, and states that participation must be voluntary. The Department declined to mandate a specific form (e.g., written consent), but recognizes recipients may obtain written consent and must provide the information needed for informed consent per §106.44(k)(3). Additional safeguards apply for minors, including parental/guardian rights under §106.6(g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice requirements prior to initiating informal resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must provide notice describing the allegations, the requirements of the informal resolution process, the right to withdraw and to initiate or resume grievance procedures prior to agreeing to a resolution, the effect of entering into a resolution agreement, the potential terms of a resolution agreement, and information the recipient will maintain and could disclose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.44(k)(3) was revised: paragraph (v) now requires notice of potential terms that may be requested or offered (including that agreements are binding only on the parties); paragraph (vi) requires notice of what information the recipient will maintain and whether/how it could be disclosed if grievance procedures are initiated or resumed. The Department deleted proposed paragraphs (vii) (limiting access to IR-obtained information) and (viii) (facilitator as witness). Notice aims to ensure parties can give informed voluntary consent without over-formalizing the IR process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitator qualifications, training, and impartiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Informal resolution facilitators must be trained and must not have a conflict of interest or bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final §106.44(k) requires facilitators (including Title IX Coordinators or designees when so assigned) to be free from conflicts of interest and bias and to be properly trained. The Department recognizes recipients may structure training and selection but insists on these basic safeguards to prevent unfair outcomes and power imbalance exploitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on using informal resolution as a means to avoid records
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must document and retain records of the informal resolution process under §106.44(k) as well as grievance procedures under §106.45 and, if applicable, §106.46, per §106.8(f)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A recipient cannot avoid creating records of sex discrimination by steering matters into informal resolution; recordkeeping requirements prevent IR from being used to obscure formal records. Recipients must comply with §106.8(f) record retention and documentation obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds and guardrails for declining informal resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may decline to offer informal resolution in certain circumstances (illustrative, not exhaustive), including when there is risk of future harm to others, repeated allegations against the same respondent, evidence of coercion or significant power differentials, or other fact-specific concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.44(k)(1)(ii) was clarified to be illustrative ('include but are not limited to'). The Department emphasizes recipients retain discretion to decline IR to fulfill obligations to address sex discrimination, similar to discretion to initiate grievance procedures absent a complaint. Recipients have flexibility to structure assessments (e.g., weigh prior violent conduct, credible threats). The Dept declined to require written explanations for declining IR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to withdraw and to initiate/resume grievance procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party has the right to withdraw from the informal resolution process and to initiate or resume the recipient's grievance procedures prior to agreeing to a resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.44(k)(3)(iii) already makes this clear and the Department declined to alter it. An agreed resolution at the conclusion of IR precludes initiating/resuming grievance procedures arising from the same allegations, but continuing sex discrimination after IR is not covered by the agreement and may be addressed through grievance procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on binding effect of IR agreements (binding only on parties)
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must advise the parties that an informal resolution agreement is binding only on the parties and cannot bind non-parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.44(k)(3)(v) was modified to clarify this point to prevent parties from agreeing to terms that depend on non-parties (e.g., requiring another person to undergo training). The notice need not list every possible term but should provide a general framework so parties can consent informedly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information maintenance and disclosure about IR records
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must explain to the parties what information related to informal resolution it may maintain and whether and how it could disclose such information if grievance procedures are initiated or resumed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department revised §106.44(k)(3)(vi) to require this notice; this balances the parties' need to understand potential consequences of IR with recipient flexibility. The Department struck earlier proposed absolute confidentiality language and the separate proposed rule about limiting access to IR-obtained information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitator cannot be treated as automatic witness in later grievance (deleted permissive allowance)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department deleted the proposed paragraph that would have permitted an informal resolution facilitator to serve as a witness if grievance procedures were resumed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters raised concerns that allowing facilitators to be witnesses would create conflicts of interest, chill IR use, and conflict with other provisions. The Department determined this provision was inapposite given §106.44(k)(3)(vi) changes and removed the facilitator-as-witness proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator duties upon notification
rubrics_metrics.description: When notified of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination, the Title IX Coordinator must take enumerated actions to promptly and effectively end any sex discrimination in its education program or activity, prevent its recurrence, and remedy its effects, including taking 'other appropriate prompt and effective steps.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These obligations (per §106.44(f)(1)) provide context for IR: recipients may resolve identifiable policies/practices under §106.44(f)(1) and Title IX Coordinators may delegate duties, but must ensure prompt effective responses. The Coordinator's duties inform when IR may be appropriate vs. when formal procedures are needed to fulfill obligations to end discrimination.
